summary: Patricia Fister is a scholar of Japanology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Kansas (~1978–1983), where she served as assistant professor of art history (~1983–1990), and later was professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (~2007–2019).

Patricia Schiaffini-Vedani works in Sinology and Tibetology. She completed graduate studies at Peking University (1990–1994) under Zhao Zumo, Zhuhong Zhang, and Shufen Mu, and earned her Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania under Perry Link.
Patrick Arthur Pranke is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Michigan (attested 2004) under the supervision of Luis O. Gómez and Victor B. Lieberman.

Patrick McAllister is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna (~2004–2011) under doctoral supervisor Helmut Krasser and teachers Karin Preisendanz and Ernst Steinkellner.

Patrick Olivelle is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. He studied at the University of Oxford (~1969–1972) and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania (~1972–1974) under Ludo Rocher. He held posts at Indiana University (1974–1991) and the University of Texas at Austin (from 1991).
Patrick R. Uhlmann is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He was a Ph.D. candidate at the University of California, Los Angeles (attested 2012), where he studied under Robert E. Buswell Jr.

Patrul Rinpoche was a Tibetan Buddhist scholar and philosopher. He studied under numerous masters, including Jigme Gyelwai Nyugu (~1828–1842), Zhabkar Tsokdruk Rangdrol, and Do Khyentse Yeshe Dorje, and became a renowned teacher whose students included Shenpen Nangwa and Shechen Gyaltsab.

Pattaratorn Chirapravati is a scholar of archaeology and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. at Cornell University (~1991–1994) and served on the faculty at California State University, Sacramento (2002–2016), after positions at Silpakorn University, Tsukuba, and the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco.

Paul B. Donnelly is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral work under Geshe Lhundub Sopa (attested 1997) alongside traditional training with Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe and Lobsang Gyatso, and held a post at Northern Arizona University.

Paul Bernard was an archaeologist and specialist in Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the École Normale Supérieure and the Sorbonne, he directed the Délégation Archéologique Française en Afghanistan (1965–1980) and held chairs at the CNRS and École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Paul Carus was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Tübingen (~1874–1876), taught at Kriegsschule Dresden (~1876–1881), and worked at the Open Court Publishing Company (~1887–1919).

Paul Copp specializes in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Massachusetts Amherst and earned his Ph.D. at Princeton University under Stephen F. Teiser (attested 2005), later holding posts at Western Michigan University and the University of Chicago.
Paul Courtright is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He held academic posts at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro and at Emory University (attested 1998).

Paul Crowe is a scholar of religious studies and Sinology. He pursued graduate studies at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura and Daniel L. Overmyer, and held a professorship at Simon Fraser University (attested 2010).

Paul David Devanandan was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. Educated at Presidency College and Yale University (doctorate ~1928–1931), he served as professor at United Theological College (1932–1949) and director of the Christian Institute for the Study of Religion and Society (1956).

Paul David Numrich is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Michigan in 1992 and held posts at the Theological Consortium of Greater Columbus and Loyola University Chicago (attested 2006).

Paul Debes was a German scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He founded the Buddhistisches Seminar (1948), co-founded and served on the board of the Buddhistische Gesellschaft Hamburg (1954), and founded the Deutsche Buddhistische Union (1955).

Paul Demiéville was a Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot. He held posts at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient, INALCO, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and was professor at the Collège de France (1946–1964).

Paul Deussen was an Indologist and philosopher educated at Bonn, Tübingen, and Berlin, where he studied under Christian Lassen. He taught as a Privatdozent in Geneva and Berlin, and became a professor at Kiel University in 1889.
Paul Dundas was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. Educated at the University of Edinburgh, he led Asian studies there (~1976–2017) and later headed the Pali Text Society (~2004–2023).
